# Frozen official historical processing corpus

These offline integration tests cover four documented layout transitions:

| System | Official Acre files | What is checked |
|---|---|---|
| SINASC | `DNRAC1995.dbc`, `DNAC1996.DBC` | Different birth-date formats, sex labels and gestation code domains |
| SIH-RD | `RDAC9712.dbc`, `RDAC9801.dbc` | Two/four-digit competence years, six/eight-digit dates, counts and money |
| SIA-PA | `PAAC9910.DBC`, `PAAC9911.dbc` | Four/six-digit reference months, management labels, counts and money |
| CNES-SR | `SRAC0802.dbc`, `SRAC0803.dbc` | Historical/current DBF service descriptions, adjacent service/classification keys, leading zeros and missing counts |

Each input contains the first three source records and only the fields listed
in `manifest.csv`. These are real source values, not invented observations.
Personal identifiers, addresses and unrelated fields are omitted. DBC headers
are reduced to the selected columns and record count; retained cell bytes and
physical column order are unchanged. The body is re-encoded as literal DCL
tokens with a new CRC32. These small inputs are not byte-for-byte copies of the
full downloadable DBCs and do not replace the full-file reader corpus.

The corresponding DEF and required CNV/DBF members retain their exact official
contents. Unused members are omitted, and directory prefixes are normalized to
portable ASCII paths. `dictionary-members.csv` records each member checksum and
the original ZIP member name as hexadecimal bytes. ZIP-name encoding itself is
covered separately by the parser unit tests.

## Independent expected results

`raw.csv` is generated using the legacy DBC-to-DBF converter and
`foreign::read.dbf()`, not the direct reader. `expected.csv` was transcribed
after inspecting the raw records and physical official dictionary definitions;
it is not generated by any `process_*()` function or conversion helper.

- The 1995 SINASC DEF uses `GESTACAO.CNV`: code `4` is `37-41 semanas`.
  The current definition used for 1996 references `SEMANAS.CNV`: code `5` is
  `37 a 41`. The separate current `GESTACAO.CNV` is not that DEF's relation.
- The selected SINASC sex labels differ between its two official dictionaries.
- Both SIH definitions map sex `1` to `Masculino`. Dates and decimal monetary
  values were checked against the source records, independently of conversion.
- SIA's applicable `TPGESTAO.CNV` maps `MP` and `PB` to the descriptions recorded
  in `expected.csv`; `TPGEST_C.CNV` is retained so relation selection is tested.
- CNES expectations come from exact DBF keys `024103`, `024104`, `061162` in
  `S_CLASSEA.DBF` and `111001`, `141001`, `141002` in `S_CLASSEN.DBF`.

Tests verify raw values, processed values, output classes, category counts,
unknown/coercion diagnostics and dictionary selection in all three label modes.
The same expectations are also applied after combining the two periods of each
system. Both CNES key columns are retained adjacent to each other.

This establishes agreement for these selected cases, not every historical
record or independent TabWin/TabNet execution. The downloadable dictionaries
were retrieved for this corpus in September 2026; their original publication
dates are not inferred from the dates of the DBC observations.

## Rebuild and audit

From the repository root:

```sh
Rscript data-raw/build-historical-fixtures.R
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "historical-fixtures", stop_on_failure = TRUE)'
```

The builder obtains missing originals from the exact URLs in `manifest.csv`
and verifies their SHA-256 hashes before rebuilding. Files already in
`.cache/review-history` are reused only if they match those pins. An unavailable
or replaced original must be recovered independently; do not replace the pin
just to make a regression pass. The offline test suite does not contact DataSUS.

Changing expected results requires a separate review of source records and
dictionary rules. The builder never rewrites `expected.csv`. Sources are the
Brazilian Ministry of Health/DataSUS public dissemination archives, individually
attributed by URL and checksum in the manifest.

The corpus CSV files use LF line endings, enforced by `.gitattributes`, so a
Windows checkout does not change their pinned checksums. Integrity checks always
hash the exact bytes; they do not normalize a changed file before comparison.
